SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, John 11:43: "When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”"

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord; Lazarus of Bethany; Martha; Crowd in John

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.
- Lazarus of Bethany: man in his thirties; lean, medium build; olive skin weathered by sun; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard, streaked grey at the chin; calm, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown, with a dark wool cloak in earth-brown. Carries no props.
- Martha of Bethany: a woman in her thirties, of sturdy and capable build, with warm olive skin weathered by sun. Dark brown hair is covered by a plain linen head veil pulled back from a careful face with a firm mouth and tired, attentive eyes. Her signature outfit, worn most often, is an undyed ochre-brown tunic with a rust-red wool cloak over the shoulders, belted with a plain cord. She carries no signature props.
- Crowd in John: adults and some older children of Jewish and Gentile communities in Galilee and Judea, ages roughly 15 to 60; lean to sturdy build; olive to tan skin; dark or grey-streaked hair kept short or tied back, beards kept trimmed or unshaven among the men; plain, weathered faces showing the sun and labour. Signature outfit: a undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, earth brown or faded blue, with a long woollen cloak in dusty ochre, worn over the shoulders. Carries nothing alone.
- Joseph of Arimathea's new tomb: a rock-cut tomb in a garden outside Jerusalem, hewn into a limestone hillside with a low doorway. A large round stone stands ready to be rolled against the door. Pale grey-cream rock, olive trees and a few flowering shrubs, stone-paved ground, dry scrub and a cut ledge within for the body. No people.
- Only Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord, Lazarus of Bethany, Martha, Crowd in John, Joseph of Arimathea's new tomb have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

Action: Jesus cries out in a loud voice, calling Lazarus forth from the tomb.
Setting: Rock-cut tomb entrance on a hillside outside Bethany, with a stone village beyond.
Secondary elements: Martha standing near Jesus with her head bowed in expectation; a crowd of villagers and mourners gathered at a distance on the rocky slope; the dark tomb mouth with a stone rolled aside.
Mood: Tense, hushed expectancy with reverent awe.
Time of day: Late afternoon, shifting toward dusk, clear dry air, warm low sunlight slanting across the rocky ground with deep shadow inside the tomb.
Composition: Wide view from the slope below, Jesus centered before the tomb mouth with Martha beside him and the crowd spread in the middle distance.

ART STYLE: Fresco
Rendering: A finished early Renaissance fresco-style painting of the work's world: calm, monumental figures, clear gestures and simple architecture, painted in soft matte color.
Negatives: Show the scene itself, never a wall, plaster cracks, painted border, frame or ornamental band. No letters or inscriptions anywhere, and halos, if any, are plain. Avoid photorealism and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Soft earth reds, ochres, sage greens and pale lapis blue on light grounds.
Lighting: Even, gentle daylight with soft modelling and few cast shadows.
Materials and texture: Matte, chalky paint surface within the depicted world.
Composition: Balanced, legible staging with figures in a shallow space; the scene painted out to every edge and corner.

- Goliath: man of enormous height, over nine feet tall, broad-shouldered and heavily muscled, around forty years old. Olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a full dark beard, strong heavy brow, grave and hard features. Wears bronze scale armour over a linen tunic, bronze greaves, and a bronze helmet, colours of bronze, dark leather and undyed linen. Typical dress: a knee-length woven tunic of undyed wool with a bordered hem in blue or red, a leather belt and a short cloak of dark wool. Signature props: a bronze helmet with a crest and a round shield, carried by the army; no props carried by the figure alone.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, 1 Samuel 17:49: "David put his hand in his bag, took a stone and slung it, and struck the Philistine in his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: David son of Jesse (king of Israel); Goliath; Philistines

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.
- Goliath: man of enormous height, over nine feet tall, broad-shouldered and heavily muscled, around forty years old. Olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a full dark beard, strong heavy brow, grave and hard features. Wears bronze scale armour over a linen tunic, bronze greaves, and a bronze helmet, colours of bronze, dark leather and undyed linen. Carries a great spear with a heavy iron head and a sword at his side.
- Valley of Elah: a broad, shallow valley of the Judean lowlands between rounded hills of terraced limestone, with a dry watercourse winding through its floor. Scattered terebinth and oak trees and low scrub grow along the slopes, and sun-baked earth shows pale between rocks. Rough stone walls and simple dwellings of field stone mark the hill ridges.
- Philistines: adult men of the coastal cities, age twenty to forty; medium-to-broad build, sun-browned skin; close-cropped dark hair and a short beard; calm, hard-set features, not caricatured. Typical dress: a knee-length woven tunic of undyed wool with a bordered hem in blue or red, a leather belt and a short cloak of dark wool. Signature props: a bronze helmet with a crest and a round shield, carried by the army; no props carried by the figure alone.
- Only David son of Jesse (king of Israel), Goliath, Valley of Elah, Philistines have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: David, a young shepherd in a tunic, standing with his sling still swinging low at his side after the release.
Action: The stone has just struck Goliath's forehead, and the giant is toppling forward, face first, toward the dry earth.
Setting: Dry wadi floor of the Valley of Elah, scattered stones and scrub, open ground between the two battle lines.
Secondary elements: Goliath in bronze scale armor and helmet, falling; Philistine soldiers in the distance at a standstill; Israelite soldiers watching from their ridge.
Mood: Tense, sudden and awe-struck, with grief and hope held in a single breath.
Time of day: Midday, bright sun, clear dry air, harsh direct light casting short shadows.
Composition: Wide view from the side at ground level, David small but central on the left, Goliath mid-fall on the right, the valley stretching behind both.

ART STYLE: Fresco
Rendering: A finished early Renaissance fresco-style painting of the work's world: calm, monumental figures, clear gestures and simple architecture, painted in soft matte color.
Negatives: Show the scene itself, never a wall, plaster cracks, painted border, frame or ornamental band. No letters or inscriptions anywhere, and halos, if any, are plain. Avoid photorealism and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Soft earth reds, ochres, sage greens and pale lapis blue on light grounds.
Lighting: Even, gentle daylight with soft modelling and few cast shadows.
Materials and texture: Matte, chalky paint surface within the depicted world.
Composition: Balanced, legible staging with figures in a shallow space; the scene painted out to every edge and corner.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)'s reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for David son of Jesse (king of Israel) only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: When the Philistine arose, and walked and came near to meet David, David hurried and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
- After: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and struck the Philistine and killed him; but there was no sword in David’s hand.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

But Yahweh isn't in the cast list at all, and divine depiction rules forbid giving God a human face or body—so a standing human shepherd figure with a staff might be flagging an embodied-divine-figure problem even though Yahweh technically has no cast entry to match against, since missing_canon and embodied_formless both seem like imperfect fits here.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A flock of sheep lying down together on the green grass
Action: Sheep settling to rest in lush pasture while a shepherd stands watch nearby
Setting: Green hill pasture near a village in ancient Judah, with a still pool and a low stone enclosure
Secondary elements: A shepherd in a simple undyed wool tunic and cloak with a staff, a still pool reflecting the sky, scattered sheep grazing
Mood: Peaceful, calm and restful, with quiet trust
Time of day: Early morning, still cool air, light mist over the grass, soft golden sunrise light
Composition: Wide view from slightly above the hillside, the flock in the foreground and the still water and village beyond

ART STYLE: Gouache
Rendering: A finished gouache painting of the work's world: opaque, matte color laid in confident flat shapes with soft painted edges, like a mid-century illustrated Bible, not a sketch.
Negatives: Paint covers the whole picture, sky and corners included: no paper margins, unpainted edges, border or frame, and no sheet of paper or book page. Avoid cartoon caricature, comic-book styling, photorealism and digital airbrush smoothness.
Palette: Warm, saturated earth colors with deep blues and greens; clear light-and-shade masses.
Lighting: Simple, warm, directional light; shadows as flat cool shapes.
Materials and texture: Matte opaque paint with visible brush marks and slight dry-brush texture, within the depicted world.
Composition: Clear, readable staging with the key figures large; the setting painted out to every edge and corner.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: A Psalm by David. Yahweh is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.
- After: He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).
